decision.detail: Zip the camera bag shut. The reel's in it. It stays in it. Turn from the Rialto doorway. Walk. The evening air is cold and smells like wet brick. I pass the ballroom on the left — the lights are on, gold and stupid and beautiful, someone's already got a drink in their hand through the window. I don't look in. I keep walking. The station line hums under the sidewalk. I can feel it in the soles of my boots. I don't stop for it. I walk to the hotel. I sit in the lobby. The crew's there. Coffee. I don't ask for a cup. I sit. The bag is at my feet. I don't open it. I don't deliver the reel. Rita's got hers on the patch. Mine's mine. I watch the coffee go cold in the cups I didn't pour. Phil's at nine. Rita's not here. The Rialto's going dark and the lights over there are going to stay on till someone turns them off and I don't care which. I'm done. One take. She talked to her girl. The charge died mid-sentence and that's the ending. I don't fix it. I don't screen it. I sit in the lobby and I let the evening be the evening.
decision.intention: Get to the lobby. Sit. Don't touch the reel. Let the night go on without me in it.
decision.words: Silence. Maybe one breath out, slow, through the nose, when I pass the ballroom. Not a word. Just the air leaving.
